newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt's Mubarak invites Israel's Peres.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak invites Israel's Peres.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, while refusing to meet Israel's hardline prime minister, has invited its opposition leader Shimon Peres to meet him in Egypt next week, a spokeswoman for Peres said on Sunday.

Mubarak said on Saturday that he told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu the two leaders would not meet until Israel resolved with the Palestinians its long-delayed pullback from the West Bank town of Hebron.

The spokeswoman said a date had yet to be set for the meeting between Mubarak and Peres but it would take place next week. Mubarak will meet Israeli President Ezer Weizman, whose job is largely ceremonial, in Egypt on Monday.

Peres, ousted as prime minister by Likud leader Netanyahu in May elections, will hold talks on Sunday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the Israeli-blockaded West Bank town of Nablus at 1200 GMT, the spokeswoman said.
Netanyahu's spokesman said the prime minister had agreed to the talks between Peres and Arafat, who last met on August 22.
The Hebron redeployment should have been carried out in March but was delayed by Peres after Islamic militant suicide bombings killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.

It was frozen by Netanyahu. He says changes are needed to ensure the security of 400 Jewish settlers living in Hebron, which has a population of 100,000 Arabs. The Palestinians refuse to amend the Hebron accord.
